title: Source tax tariff: denomination, spouse employment and tariff code
purpose: Ask the denomination, whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed and whether the employee has children, then compute the full Zurich tariff code (letter, child digit and church-tax suffix) or the result shown when no code applies.

stories.title: Ask the religious denomination only where source tax needs it and derive the church-tax suffix
stories.i_want: the denomination of every employee who needs a Zurich tariff code, reduced to the two groups the calculator uses, and the church-tax suffix worked out from it
stories.so_that: the tariff code ends in the right church-tax suffix (Y or N), and employees who need no tariff code are not asked about their religion
stories.priority_reason: Without the denomination Lonio cannot complete the tariff code it computes in place of HR (D-001). HR also needs source tax questions asked only of the employees who are subject to source tax (F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only of employees who need a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee filling in step 6 'Source tax details' of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to ask for the denomination
acceptance_criteria.then: The denomination is asked, and is required, only if the employee is subject to source tax. It is not asked of an employee living in Liechtenstein who returns home daily, or who does not return daily but expects at most 45 non-return days, because that person is in principle not liable and the tariff questions are skipped. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the Liechtenstein questions come before the denomination (D-040). No one else is asked. The answer is recorded for HR to determine the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination offers only the calculator's two groups
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee chooses exactly one of two answers: 'Roman Catholic, Christ Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' or 'None or other'. No more specific religion is asked or recorded, because the calculator only distinguishes these two groups.

acceptance_criteria.title: Church-tax suffix follows the denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who answered the denomination
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the church-tax suffix of the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: 'Roman Catholic, Christ Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' gives the suffix Y. 'None or other' gives the suffix N.

stories.title: Ask married employees and registered partners subject to source tax whether their spouse or partner works
stories.i_want: to know whether the spouse or registered partner of a married employee subject to source tax is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: the tariff letter is B or C as the calculator decides
stories.priority_reason: HR names this as a calculator question that changes the result for married employees (F-hr_transcript-6a0a40). Without it Lonio cannot compute the tariff code (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is asked only of married employees and registered partners who need a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee filling in step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to ask if the spouse or partner works
acceptance_criteria.then: The question is asked, and is required, only if the employee is subject to source tax, is not a Liechtenstein resident who is in principle not liable, and is Married or in a Registered partnership. Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated employees are not asked. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-003): for source tax a registered partnership counts as married and Separated counts as single, as in the calculator. The answer is recorded for HR to determine the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Meaning and answers of the spouse employment question
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse employment question is asked
acceptance_criteria.then: The employee answers 'yes' if the spouse or registered partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income, and 'no' otherwise. Only 'yes' and 'no' are possible. Separated employees are not asked, even though their spouse's date of birth is collected for the pension fund.

stories.title: Ask employees subject to source tax whether they have children
stories.i_want: to know whether an employee who needs a tariff code has biological or adopted children
stories.so_that: the child questions are asked only when there are children, and the child digit and an H tariff can be worked out
stories.priority_reason: The child digit is part of every tariff code Lonio computes (D-001, F-zh_source_tax_calculator-4c53e3). Asking only employees subject to source tax follows HR's request (F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Children question is asked only of employees who need a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee filling in step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to ask about children
acceptance_criteria.then: The question is asked, and is required, whatever the civil status, only if the employee is subject to source tax and is not a Liechtenstein resident who is in principle not liable. No one else is asked. The answer is recorded for HR to determine the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Which children count for the question and what the answer opens
acceptance_criteria.then: Married employees and registered partners are asked whether they or their spouse or partner have biological or adopted children. All other employees are asked whether they have biological or adopted children. Only 'yes' and 'no' are possible. 'yes' opens step 7 'Children' with one block per child and no maximum number of children (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert). 'no' skips step 7, and the child digit of the tariff code is 0.

stories.title: Derive the base source tax tariff letter
stories.i_want: Lonio to work out the base tariff letter (A, B, C or H) from the civil status, the spouse's employment and the children, following the calculator
stories.so_that: I no longer have to click through the Zurich calculator to find the tariff for each employee subject to source tax
stories.priority_reason: The base letter is the core of the tariff code that replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001, F-hr_transcript-34494f).

acceptance_criteria.title: Married employees and registered partners get C or B
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who needs a tariff code and is Married or in a Registered partnership (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert: a registered partnership counts as married for source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: The letter is C if the spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income, and B if not. Children do not change the letter.

acceptance_criteria.title: No tariff for replacement income
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee who needs a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio assumes earned income for every new employee. It does not ask the income type, and the base letter is never G.

stories.title: Replace the base letter with the cross-border letter where the cross-border tariff applies
stories.i_want: Lonio to turn the base letter into the cross-border letter for employees living in Germany to whom the cross-border tariff applies
stories.so_that: cross-border commuters such as those living in Konstanz get the correct tariff without HR working through the calculator's Germany questions
stories.priority_reason: HR finds the cross-border questions the hardest part of the calculator (F-hr_transcript-8595fb), and Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border letter when the cross-border tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany to whom the cross-border tariff applies: either they return home daily and have a certificate of residence, or they do not return daily, a daily return would be reasonable, and they expect at most 60 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: The base letter is replaced: A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N and H becomes P. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-051): the mapping follows the calculator in full, so G would become Q, but G cannot occur in onboarding (D-006).

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter kept when the cross-border tariff does not apply
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who needs a tariff code and to whom the cross-border tariff does not apply: they live in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany, or they live in Germany and return daily without a certificate of residence ('no' or 'not yet'), or they do not return daily and a daily return is not reasonable, or they expect more than 60 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: The tariff letter is the base letter unchanged. 'Not yet' for the certificate of residence counts as 'no' (D-035).

stories.title: Compute and record the full source tax tariff code
stories.i_want: Lonio to compute the full Zurich tariff code (tariff letter, number of counted children and church-tax suffix) for every employee subject to source tax, or to state clearly why there is no code
stories.so_that: I get the tariff code without clicking through the calculator myself, and I can see straight away which employees need no code or need my attention
stories.priority_reason: This is the product decision to replace HR's manual calculator step (D-001). HR uses the Zurich calculator for everybody today (F-hr_transcript-34494f).

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code is one text of letter, child digit and suffix
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who is not a Liechtenstein resident in principle not liable, and who has answered every question the code depends on
acceptance_criteria.then: The code is a single text: the tariff letter, then the number of children counted in step 7 'Children', then the church-tax suffix, for example 'C1Y', 'L0Y' or 'A0N'. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-051): this is the format of the code. The code is recorded for HR.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents in principle not liable get the treaty notice instead of a code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein who returns home daily, or who does not return daily but expects at most 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: Instead of a tariff code the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement'. It is flagged for HR; how HR sees the flag is part of the later HR-side spec (D-034). The denomination, spouse employment and children questions are not asked. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-040): this order and skipping apply.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days get the plain code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein who does not return home daily and expects more than 45 non-return days

acceptance_criteria.title: Incomplete code after an HR change
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax for whom an answer the code needs is missing, for example because HR changed an answer after submission and a question now applies that the employee was never asked
acceptance_criteria.then: The result is 'incomplete - HR must complete' instead of a code until HR enters the missing answers. The questionnaire stays read-only for the employee and is not reopened. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-048, D-053).

acceptance_criteria.title: Code always follows the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: a submitted questionnaire whose answers HR later changes (for example a move, a marriage, a new child or a certificate of residence handed in later)
acceptance_criteria.when: the tariff code is looked at again
acceptance_criteria.then: The code is always worked out again from the latest answers. Answers that no longer apply are discarded. No earlier code is kept.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unexplored calculator paths are checked before go-live
acceptance_criteria.given: tariff codes for paths not observed in the calculator: more than 3 counted children (for example H3N or P3N and above), the inferred per-child results, and the residence block for A, B and H
acceptance_criteria.then: Before go-live a domain expert compares Lonio's computed codes with the calculator for these paths. This is a non-blocking go-live condition (see OQ-calculator-coverage). Where a calculator result has been observed, it wins over the general rule (assumption D-046). Special tariffs such as D (second job) are out of scope.
